title: Perf bench: latency & throughput runs - Riley Thompson - 2026-03-16
content:
Context:
- Quick scratchpad for latency/throughput runs I did on 2026-03-16. Goal: validate recent runtime changes (v1.9.2) around continuous batching + improved KV-cache warm path and int8 execution. These are informal notes - will extract cleaned numbers for a proper perf doc if the team wants them.

Environment:
- HW: Dedicated pool (dev-reserved) - single A100 80GB (node with 1x GPU used).
- Runtime: serving-runtime v1.9.2 (local build from PR #432).
- Models: redwood-alpha-7b (fp16), redwood-alpha-7b-int8 (GPTQ-like quant), redwood-alpha-13b-fp16 (one sanity check).
- OS/driver: Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.1, NCCL 2.18.
- Benchmark harness: rwi-bench (internal script) + small JMeter clients for concurrency curves.
- Notes: tests run on isolated node, network minimal noise, but not a full CI reproducible environment.

Commands used (examples):
- rwi-bench --model redwood-alpha-7b --variant fp16 --seq 512 --gen 128 --batch 1 --concurrency 1 --requests 200
- rwi-bench --model redwood-alpha-7b-int8 --seq 512 --gen 128 --batch 8 --concurrency 8 --requests 1000 --kv-cache warm
- jmeter --testfile perf/concurrency-plan.jmx --threads 32 --duration 300s (for saturation tests)

What I measured (high-level):
- Latency numbers are end-to-end (client->server->client) measured at the client. Generation time includes decode loop.
- Throughput reported as tokens/sec aggregated across all workers during steady-state window (after 30s warmup).

Selected runs (summary):
1) Baseline: redwood-alpha-7b fp16, batch=1, concurrency=1, KV cold (first request)
   - p50: 0.96s, p95: 1.7s, avg tokens/sec: 95
   - notes: cold KV includes model init + first KV cache fill; latency dominated by initial decode.

2) Warm KV (same config)
   - p50: 0.36s, p95: 0.62s, avg tokens/sec: 310
   - notes: warming KV cache drops p95 by ~63% for repeated contexts. Expected behavior; confirms warm path optimizations in v1.9.2.

3) Batching effect: fp16, batch=8, concurrency=8, KV warm
   - p50 (per-request): 0.48s, p95: 0.9s
   - aggregate throughput: 3,900 tokens/sec (steady state)
   - per-request latency increased vs batch=1 p50 but throughput scaled ~12x vs single concurrency run.

4) int8 quant variant: redwood-alpha-7b-int8, batch=8, concurrency=8, KV warm
   - p50: 0.42s, p95: 0.83s, throughput: 4,350 tokens/sec
   - memory: ~28GB GPU memory used vs ~36GB for fp16.
   - notes: int8 improved throughput ~12% and reduced GPU memory allowing larger batches. Small but visible improvement; need eval on output quality for customer-facing use.

5) Tail latency stress: fp16, batch=8, concurrency=32 (push to saturation)
   - errors: occasional 503s when queue exceeded threshold (we hit runtime queue limit), median latency sliding up
   - p50: 0.76s, p95: 1.8s, 99th: 3.4s
   - recycler: observed that enabling adaptive fallback (drop to smaller batch or route to fallback variant) would be useful to keep tail bounded.

6) 13B sanity check (fp16), batch=1, concurrency=2 (KV warm)
   - p50: 0.74s, p95: 1.6s, throughput: 210 tokens/sec
   - notes: expectedly higher latency; 13B not fully optimized on single A100 for large batches.

Observations / quick conclusions:
- KV cache warm path in v1.9.2 is behaving well; warm p95 decreased ~60% vs cold. This is the biggest single win for conversational workloads where context reuse is high.
- Batching increases aggregate tokens/sec significantly (x10+ at batch 8) but increases per-request tail latency; for SLOs with tight tail we need to cap batch size or use per-route policies (small batch or direct low-latency routing).
- int8 quant gives modest throughput and memory improvements. Worth enabling as an opt-in profile for Dedicated customers who prioritize unit cost; however need automated quality checks (evals) before promoting widely.
- Under high concurrency, runtime queueing becomes the limiting factor and leads to 503s. We should evaluate adaptive admission control + immediate fallback to smaller batch variants to reduce 99th percentile.
- Streaming (not instrumented in these runs) is likely to show better p50 for perceived latency (start-of-stream) even if overall token throughput is similar - plan to run streaming-specific experiments next.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Run repeat experiments with multi-GPU (NVLink) and scaled Dedicated pool to validate scaling curve.
- Add objective quality eval for int8 variant (existing eval harness, tie to PR). TODO: link eval job.
- Create small chart pack: latency_vs_batch.png, throughput_vs_concurrency.png (I sketched locally; will export final images and attach to a cleaned PR).
- Add a stress test with adaptive fallback enabled to measure tail improvements.
- Share results with SRE/Runtime team; propose a short follow-up to test admission control heuristics (PERF-1283).

Notes-to-self/questions:
- Did I accidentally leave continuous-batching disabled for some runs? Need to re-check run logs (rwi-bench --log).
- Try enabling smaller batch cap for route /chat/low-latency and measure real-user p95 emulation.
- Coordinate with Maya for the int8 quality checks (ask Maya for sample prompts + reference outputs).

Attachments (local):
- ~/bench/2026-03-16/latency_vs_batch.png (generate export)
- ~/bench/2026-03-16/throughput_vs_concurrency.csv (raw numbers)

Raw command outputs (snippet):
- fp16 batch=8 warm: avg tokens/sec 3898, p95 0.90s
- int8 batch=8 warm: avg tokens/sec 4352, p95 0.83s

If anyone wants the raw logs or wants me to re-run with a different config (multi-GPU / streaming / different seq lengths) ping me (Riley).

End of scratchpad.
